MODULE 01 Is a Café Right for You?
5–7 Min Video / Article +
Sample Lesson Script Excerpt:

"Welcome. Opening a café sounds glamorous—great coffee, loyal customers, your own vibrant space. The reality is early mornings, long days, high fixed costs, and constant operational demands. This module helps you decide honestly whether this is the right path.

Key questions: Are you prepared for 50–60+ hour weeks, especially in year one? Do you enjoy people, problem-solving under pressure, and attention to detail? Is morning and day-trade (coffee, breakfast, light lunch) the model that fits your lifestyle? Completing this program gives you the full picture before committing capital."

Quiz Question 1: Most café owners work standard 40-hour weeks once established. True or False?
Answer: False. The early years typically require 50–60+ hours of operational and oversight commitment.
Quiz Question 2: What is a major advantage of focusing on morning and day trade?
A) Lower evening staffing costs & shorter operational windows
B) No need for compliance
C) Guaranteed high liquor margins
Answer: A — Lower evening staffing costs, simplified shifts, and focused daytime customer turnover.
MODULE 02 Business Planning & Realistic Financials
Financial Modeling + Spreadsheet +
Key Financial Principles:
  • Cape Town Startup Range: R620,000 to R1,780,000+ for an 80–120 m² shop.
  • Working Capital: Always maintain 3 to 6 months of operating runway to bridge to consistent profitability.
  • Target Occupancy Cost: Keep rent + utilities strictly between 6% and 10% of projected turnover.
  • Target Net Margin: Well-run cafés achieve ~10% net profit; coffee gross margins (~75-80%) must carry food preparation overheads.
Quiz Question: What is a healthy rent-to-turnover occupancy ratio for a café?
Answer: 6% to 10% of monthly gross turnover. Exceeding 12% is one of the highest causes of café distress.
MODULE 03 Location, Zoning & Premises
Site Selection & Lease Clauses +
Key Talking Points:

Evaluating pedestrian foot traffic at 07:00 vs 13:00. Navigating landlord tenant installation allowances (TI), electrical supply (minimum 3-phase 60A for commercial espresso), plumbing access, and verifying City zoning rights (Local Business 1/2) before signing commercial leases.

MODULE 04 Legal Compliance & Certifications (Cape Town Specific)
Free CoA & City e-Services +
Cape Town Step-by-Step Compliance Checklist:
  1. Register on City of Cape Town e-Services and activate the Environmental Health portal.
  2. Draft and upload a 1:50 scale layout plan showing: designated food prep areas, scullery, refrigeration, waste disposal, hand-wash basins, and floor drains.
  3. Submit ID of Person in Charge and national food safety hygiene certificates.
  4. Ensure premises meet Regulation R638 (washable walls, insect screens, pest control logs, water temperature controls).
  5. Environmental Health Practitioner (EHP) conducts on-site inspection within ~10 working days.
  6. Apply for Category 1 Business Licence (~R25 fee) for sale and supply of meals.
Quiz Question 1: Is the Certificate of Acceptability (CoA) free in the City of Cape Town?
Answer: Yes, the CoA application is 100% free via City e-Services.
Quiz Question 2: What scale is preferred for the layout plan submitted for the CoA?
Answer: 1:50 scale (showing clear designation of food prep, hand-wash, and equipment).
MODULE 05 Equipment – Coffee Machinery & Catering
Commercial Hardware & Water +
Core Equipment Guidance:

Commercial 2-group espresso machines (such as the Wega Rover at R72,170), on-demand commercial grinders (Mythos Iris at R19,750), multi-stage carbon block and ion-exchange water filtration, Flojet bottled water booster systems (R4,478), under-counter refrigeration, and pure sine-wave backup power inverters for South African load shedding.

Quiz Question: Why is multi-stage water filtration essential for commercial espresso machines?
Answer: It prevents catastrophic limescale accumulation in heat exchangers/boilers and ensures balanced mineral extraction for superior cup clarity.
MODULE 06 Interior Design & Shop Fitting
Bar Workflow & Customer Flow +

Designing the ergonomic barista triangle (grinder → grouphead → knockbox → steam wand). Minimizing barista steps per ticket, designing customer queueing lanes away from the collection point, and durable counter surfaces that survive coffee oils and moisture.

MODULE 07 Menu Development (Coffee + Morning & Day Food)
Recipe Margins & Attach Rates +

Curating core espresso drinks, milk alternatives (oat/almond attach rates), breakfast bowls, toasties, and baked goods. Calculating recipe food cost percentages (targeting 28-32%) and locking in dependable local suppliers.

MODULE 08 Staffing, Training & Management
Barista Skills & Labor Control +

Hiring passionate baristas versus training technical precision. Food safety compliance, opening/closing cleaning checklists, espresso dial-in procedures, and managing rosters to keep labor between 25% and 35% of turnover.

MODULE 09 Operations & Odoo POS Setup
Tech Stack & Floor Plans +
Why Odoo POS is Built for Cafés:
  • Integrated Suite: Live sync between Point of Sale, Inventory deductions, CRM loyalty, and Accounting journals.
  • Café Features: Floor plan table management, custom coffee modifiers (extra shot, oat milk, decaf), kitchen display system (KDS), and offline order caching during power cuts.
  • Daily Controls: Cash register reconciliation, shift summaries, and automated reorder alerts for coffee beans and cups.
Quiz Question: Name two major benefits of an integrated Odoo POS system for a café.
Answer: Real-time inventory deduction per coffee recipe, seamless automated accounting entries, and built-in offline reliability.
MODULE 10 Marketing, Customer Experience & Growth
Neighbourhood Loyalty & Buzz +

Building hyper-local awareness in Cape Town. Free coffee soft launches for local offices and neighbours, Google Business profile optimization, Instagram storytelling around roast provenance, and digital loyalty cards.
